correctness.rationale: For every base b>=2 and progression s+id, the step divides the gcd of differences of all selected powers b^e. The power-difference gcd identity gives the geometric lower bound on the span of r one-positions, attained by s=0,d=b-1; its equality case fixes the unique critical pattern. For at least three ones, the first exponent gap f is <=floor(log_b(n-1)); the first two mark indices and f determine the factor, while nonnegative start forces j>b^f i. Counting these encodings yields the finite bound and O_b(n^2). The proof covers r=1,2 separately; finite verifier assertions are corroborative, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Arithmetic-progression subword complexity is a well-motivated invariant for automatic words. This theorem replaces the broad subexponential general bound by a quantitative quadratic bound on an entire natural lacunary family and simultaneously solves the exact maximum-density problem under arbitrary arithmetic sampling, with uniquely constrained critical patterns. Both results follow from nonlocal power-difference arithmetic and are not just prefix enumeration or a finite arbitrary slice.
